successor: Austria - Habsburg Dynasty II (Habsburg Monarchy, same Vienna court)
source1: Encyclopaedia Britannica, 'Ferdinand III, Holy Roman emperor', Britannica - https://www.britannica.com/biography/Ferdinand-III-Holy-Roman-emperor
notes: Habsburg rule from Vienna continued unbroken past 1648: Ferdinand III, archduke from 1621 and emperor 1637-1657, accepted Westphalia and was succeeded by Leopold I; Habsburgs ruled Austria 1282-1918. 1648 is a period break. Q4: Thirty Years' War, Bohemian revolt.

source1: Encyclopaedia Britannica, 'Austria: End of the Habsburg empire', Britannica - https://www.britannica.com/place/Austria/End-of-the-Habsburg-empire
source2: Encyclopaedia Britannica, 'Charles I, emperor of Austria', Britannica - https://www.britannica.com/biography/Charles-I-emperor-of-Austria
notes: After defeat in WWI, national councils acted as governments; German-Austrian state council took over central agencies in Vienna from 30 Oct; Charles renounced participation in state affairs 11 Nov 1918; republic replaced monarchy. Vienna not occupied. Alternative: T1a.

Database relabelling: Heraclius reigned in Constantinople 610-641, spanning the 631/632 break; imperial court and administration continued. Q4: army mutiny and Phocas's usurpation 602, Heraclian revolt from Carthage deposing Phocas 610.

source2: A. Shapur Shahbazi, 'Sasanian dynasty', Encyclopaedia Iranica - https://iranicaonline.org/articles/sasanian-dynasty
notes: Arabs won at Qadisiyya (636/637) and occupied Ctesiphon; Nahavand 642 ended organized resistance; Yazdegerd III killed at Merv 651 (Iranica: 650). Database 642 = Nahavand. Q4: after Khosrow II's deposition 628, ten rulers in two years.

successor: 21st Dynasty at Tanis and Theban High Priests of Amun (Thebes-Libyan Period)
source2: Encyclopaedia Britannica, 'Ancient Egypt: Egypt from 1076 BCE to the Macedonian invasion', Britannica - https://www.britannica.com/place/ancient-Egypt/Egypt-from-1076-bce-to-the-Macedonian-invasion
notes: Civil war (viceroy Pinhasy vs high priest) under Ramses XI; Herihor/Piankh ruled Thebes; at his death Egypt passed to two separate dynasties, Tanis north, Theban priests south, for over a century. Northern Tanite line arguably continuous (T0 alternative).

source1: Ulrich Theobald, 'Zhou Dynasty: The Warring States Period', ChinaKnowledge.de, 2018 - http://www.chinaknowledge.de/History/Zhou/zhou-event-zhanguo.html
source2: Xu Zhaofeng, 'Considering Chengzhou (Completion of Zhou) and Wangcheng (City of the King)', Chinese Archaeology 8 - http://www.kaogu.cn/uploads/soft/Chinese%20Archaeology/8/Considering%20Chengzhou%20%28%27Completion%20of%20Zhou%27%29%20and%20Wangcheng%20%28%27City%20of%20the%20King%27%29.pdf
notes: Qin invaded West Zhou after King Nan's death in 256 BCE, seizing the nine tripods; East Zhou occupied seven years later (249 BCE), extinguishing the Zhou house. Q4: royal domain partitioned into rival West/East Zhou branches; Warring States fragmentation.

source1: Encyclopaedia Britannica, 'Spain: Primo de Rivera (1923-30) and the Second Republic (1931-36)', Britannica - https://www.britannica.com/place/Spain/Primo-de-Rivera-1923-30-and-the-Second-Republic-1931-36
notes: Republican municipal election victory in the cities, 12 April 1931; revolutionary committee under Alcala Zamora demanded abdication; Alfonso XIII left Spain rather than face civil war; committee became provisional republican government. Q4: Primo de Rivera coup 1923, Jaca rising 1930.

successor: Ilkhanate (Mongol governors); Konya later to the Karamanids
source1: Muharrem Kesik, 'Mesud II', TDV Islam Ansiklopedisi vol. 29, 2004 - https://islamansiklopedisi.org.tr/mesud-ii
notes: Mongol vassal since Kose Dag 1243 (before W); later sultans were Ilkhanid-installed shadow rulers while Ilkhanid governors ran Anatolia; sultanate lapsed at Mesud II's death 1308. Q4: rival sultans, Baltu and Sulemis revolts, Karamanid sack of Konya 1291.

successor: Neo-Assyrian Empire, then its Saite vassal Psamtik I (26th Dynasty)
source1: Encyclopaedia Britannica, 'Ancient Egypt: Egypt from 1076 BCE to the Macedonian invasion', Britannica - https://www.britannica.com/place/ancient-Egypt/Egypt-from-1076-bce-to-the-Macedonian-invasion
notes: Esarhaddon captured Memphis 671; Ashurbanipal routed Taharqa and sacked Thebes after Tanutamon's comeback (664/663); Kushites withdrew, Psamtik I compelled Thebes to submit 656. Core taken as Egypt (Memphis); Kushite state survived in Nubia.

source2: Encyclopaedia Britannica, 'United Kingdom: Britain since 1945', Britannica - https://www.britannica.com/place/United-Kingdom/Britain-since-1945
notes: No break in London's central authority in 1968 (Wilson government continued; Labour back 1974-79); Britannica dates the empire 1601-1997. 1968 end is a period break (likely East of Suez announcement). Q4: Irish War of Independence 1919-21, Northern Ireland violence 1968.
